original_source_text: Sequential-constraint characterization consumes up to 80% of library signoff runtime. Traditional path-based methods rely on internal-node observability and fragile topology analysis, requiring extra simulations. They fail fundamentally for toggle-unexpected arcs such as hold and removal, where no robust internal voltage transitions exist. We present power-path, an internal-probe-free method that extracts a physics-grounded supply-current signature from the mandatory reference-delay simulation, enabling universal constraint estimation across all arc types without additional SPICE costs. An affine calibration using lookup table vertices refines the raw estimator for nominal characterization; for statistical deployment, an online ridge regression progressively tightens search intervals across Monte Carlo samples. Evaluated on post-layout TSMC 5 nm and 12 nm libraries across 5 PVT corners, power-path achieves 1.5× speedup with affine calibration and 3.6× with statistical calibration, while maintaining signoff-grade accuracy. The approach requires no topology analysis or additional simulations. We open-source our code and data.
